Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €9349 spend · 217 purchases
✅ What's Working
• #2 variants dominate #1s across every concept — Summer #2 (ROAS 3.56x, 70 purch), Heart Tag #2 (2.41x vs #1's 0.81x), iMessage #2 (3.03x vs #1's zero purchases). Second iterations nail the hook.
• Carousel and Video formats are the most efficient ads in the account: the unnamed Carousel hits ROAS 3.75x at €26.26 CPP, Video _ General #3 delivers ROAS 3.96x at €25.73 CPP — both beating every static on cost-per-purchase.
• Summer concept is the proven volume engine: Summer #2 alone drove 70 purchases at the highest spend level while maintaining strong ROAS, proving seasonal lifestyle framing converts this audience.
❌ What's Not Working
• Solitaire is a budget sinkhole: #1 burned €1,630 for just 24 purchases at ROAS 1.34x (CPP €67.90), and #2 spent €125 with zero purchases. The concept is dead in Belgium.
• Split concept fails both variants: #1 at ROAS 0.88x and #2 at ROAS 1.82x with CPPs above €79 — worst cost efficiency in the account. Neither variant justifies continued spend.
• #1 creative variants consistently underperform or outright fail (Heart Tag #1 ROAS 0.81x, iMessage #1 zero purchases, Catalog #1 zero purchases), suggesting first drafts lack the right hook, angle, or product framing.
⬆ Double Down On
• Carousel format: you have exactly one carousel and it's outperforming nearly everything. Build carousels for Summer, Heart Tag, and Catalog concepts immediately — this format is criminally underused.
• Video creative: Video _ General #3 is the highest-ROAS ad in the account at 3.96x on only €309 spend. Produce more video variants and give them real budget — you're leaving money on the table.
• Iterate winning concepts to #3 and #4 variants: Summer and iMessage concepts have proven product-market fit in BE. Push new angles, new hooks, new layouts within these concept families.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill Solitaire entirely — both variants are money pits, zero evidence of concept viability in Belgium. Reallocate that €1,755 immediately.
• Kill Split #1 (ROAS 0.88x, €636 spent) and Heart Tag #1 (ROAS 0.81x, €506 spent) — the #2 variants already prove the creative execution was the problem, not the product.
• Kill Heart White #1 (ROAS 0.72x) and Heart Split #1 (ROAS 1.36x) — weak Heart sub-concepts diluting spend from Heart Tag #2 which actually works.

Kamping Kitsch Club — Ads Report

7 September 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads + Google Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €2171 spend · 1146 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Urgency 'Last Call' statics are printing money — 'Static _ Last Call #1 - Copy' at 85.75x ROAS and €0.62 CPP with 121 purchases, and 'Video _ Last Call #1 - Copy' at 113.43x ROAS with 42 purchases on just €30 spend.
• Value-proposition angles ('Waar vo', 'Goedkoopste', 'Berekening') consistently convert at 20-53x ROAS with CPPs under €2.50 — rational price-justification messaging clearly resonates with this Belgian audience.
• Artist-specific callouts like 'Static _ RUBEN' deliver 34.74x ROAS at €1.79 CPP with 110 purchases — name recognition drives decisive action.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'Video _ Aftermovie #1' is a vanity trap — 8.85x ROAS looks passable but only 4 purchases at €14.1 CPP, 7-10x worse efficiency than your best statics. The video-first assumption is wrong for conversions.
• Organic repurposed content is unreliable — 'Static _ Organic #1' at 1.72x ROAS with €20.09 CPP is burning money. Not all organic content survives the jump to paid.
• Budget allocation is backwards — your top performers ('Video _ Last Call #1 - Copy' at 113x, 'Static _ Last Call #1 - Copy' at 85x) are starved at €30-€75 spend while mid-tier ads absorb 3-5x more budget.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more 'Last Call' urgency variants — different countdown windows (48h, 24h, final hours), static and short video. This angle owns your top 3 ROAS spots and has the lowest CPPs in the account.
• Create more artist-specific statics for every headliner on the lineup — the RUBEN template (110 purchases, €1.79 CPP) is a proven formula waiting to be stamped across every act.
• Build more price/value statics — 'Berekening' calculation breakdowns, 'Goedkoopste' cheapest-ticket hooks, 'Waar vo' cost-per-hour framing. Rational purchase justification is this audience's conversion trigger.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill 'Static _ Organic #1' immediately — 1.72x ROAS, 2 purchases, €20.09 CPP is pure waste with no path to profitability.
• Stop treating aftermovie video as a conversion asset — 4 purchases at €14.1 CPP belongs in a top-of-funnel awareness campaign, not your conversion objective.
• Stop underspending on winners — 'Video _ Last Call #1 - Copy' has 113x ROAS on €30 spend while 'Static _ Hart #2' at 33x gets 11x the budget. Fix allocation before producing anything new.

✅ What's Working
• Comparison ('Vergelijking') statics are the clear engine: 'Static _ Vergelijking #1 - Copy' delivers €17.81 CPR with 26 leads — best efficiency in the account. The broker-vs-kleyo savings frame resonates hard.
• 'Smart' format punches above its weight: one 'Static _ Smart #1 - Copy' variant hits €18.57 CPR with 17 results on only €316 spend — empowerment + cost-savings visual is clicking.
• Video works at moderate scale: 'General Video #1' (€566) pulls 21 results at €26.97 CPR — the only non-static format proving itself.
❌ What's Not Working
• Press/authority angle is a money pit: 'Static _ De Tijd 2' (€101.27 CPR) and its copy variant (€56.71 CPR) can't convert — brand trust creative doesn't match direct-response intent.
• Copy-paste duplication without creative iteration produces zeroes: 'General Video #1 - Copy' burned €284 for 0 results, 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy 2' burned €151 for 0 results. Cloning ≠ testing.
• Proximity ('Dichtbij #1') and the original Vergelijking #1 (no copy) both bleed at €106+ CPR — the angles or executions simply don't land.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more comparison/calculator statics with varied property price points (€250K, €400K, €500K) — the 'show the math' framework is your best performer.
• Create fresh 'Smart' format iterations: layer in social proof (number of homes sold, buyer interest stat) on top of the empowerment angle that's already converting.
• Develop more direct-response video — lead with the savings hook in the first 2 seconds, test UGC/selfie-style vs. polished formats.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all zero-result ads immediately: 'General Video #1 - Copy', 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy 2', 'Static _ Vergelijking #2 - Copy 2' (€99) — combined €534 wasted.
• Kill the 'De Tijd' authority angle entirely — neither variant breaks €55 CPR; press logos don't move homeowners to act.
• Kill 'Static _ Dichtbij #1' and 'Static _ Vergelijking #1' (original) — both above €100 CPR with negligible volume. Dead concepts.

NAOS Optics — Ads Report

7 September 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads + Google Ads + Klaviyo Email · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

25 ads · €5177 spend · 86 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Static split-format ads are the backbone: "Vuelta Split #1" (ROAS 2.46x, CPP €40.18, 17 purchases) and "Vuelta Split #2" (ROAS 2.13x, 7 purchases) drive reliable volume at efficient CPPs.
• Product-focused statics are hidden ROAS kings: "Product Ziris #2" (ROAS 4.58x, CPP €31.30) and "HelboF General #2" (ROAS 4.12x) are the best ads in the account but criminally starved of budget.
• Offer-driven statics generate volume: "Offer #1 - Copy" (18 purchases, ROAS 2.45x, CTR 110%) proves price incentives work in this price-sensitive market vs Oakley/Decathlon.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video is consistently losing to static. Four Sieben videos spent combined €1,734 at blended ROAS ~1.5x vs static average ~2.5x+. "Sieben Split #2" burned €176 with zero purchases.
• Full-image format is dead. Both "Vuelta Full" variants spent combined €372 with 2 total purchases. Split format of the same campaign converts; full doesn't.
• Before&After creatives are clickbait traps. "HelboF Before&After #1/#2" hit 158-163% CTR but generated zero purchases — training Meta's algorithm on non-buyers.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product-focused static per SKU: replicate the "Product Ziris #2" template (ROAS 4.58x) for Helbo, Selva Snow, and every colorway. Highest-returning format in the account.
• Split-format statics with offer overlays: combine the proven split layout with the offer mechanic driving "Offer #1 - Copy." Both elements convert independently; together they should compound.
• Untapped Belgian brand + prescription lens ('op sterkte') USP: zero current ads leverage the two things Oakley and Decathlon literally cannot claim. Static format, split layout, direct response CTA.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All Sieben video variants. Four ads, €1,734 combined, peak ROAS 1.87x. Static format wins this account decisively — stop funding video production.
• Vuelta Full format. Split converts, full doesn't. Two full-image variants with zero or near-zero purchases. Stop testing full-image layouts.

Netherlands

5 ads · €262 spend · 3 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Full-frame Vuelta creative converts: 'Static _ Vuelta Full #2' delivers 3.33x ROAS at a lean €34.38 CPP — best performer by far.
• Vuelta theme resonates with NL cycling audience — all 3 purchases came from Vuelta creatives.
• Engagement is sky-high across the board (CTRs above 100%), meaning the product imagery grabs attention — conversion is the bottleneck, not awareness.
❌ What's Not Working
• Split-layout creatives underperform: 'Static _ Vuelta Split #1' ate 66% of total budget (€174) at a painful 1.29x ROAS and €86.9 CPP. 'Static _ Vuelta Split #2' spent €34 with zero purchases.
• Zero creative diversity — all static, all Vuelta-themed, no video, no UGC, no product-education angles. NL market is getting one message on repeat.
• Key differentiators (prescription 'op sterkte', photochromic lenses, Belgian brand story) are completely absent from the ad mix.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more full-frame product hero statics following the 'Vuelta Full #2' template — clean single-product shots outperform busy split layouts.
• Build creatives around the prescription sports glasses angle — it's NAOS's strongest moat vs Oakley/Decathlon and has zero ad coverage.
• Introduce video formats: lens-transition demos (photochromic), on-bike POV, and quick UGC testimonials to break through static fatigue in NL feed.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop funding split-layout creatives — both split ads either bleed money or flatline. The format dilutes focus.
• Stop running an all-Vuelta, all-static creative mix in NL. One theme and one format is not a test — it's a guess.
• Stop ignoring NL-specific messaging. No Dutch copy hooks, no local social proof, no mention of shipping/returns for NL buyers.

Belgium

15 ads · €2241 spend · 154 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Catalog carousel is the volume engine — "Catalog Carousel - Espresso Coffee" drives 59 purchases at 32.73x ROAS, proving product browsing format converts this audience at scale.
• "Hold" messaging and barista education angles deliver elite efficiency — "Static _ Hold #1" (41.19x ROAS, €10.57 CPP) and "Static_Barista_Courses - Copy" (41.87x ROAS, €12.56 CPP) outperform everything on cost-per-purchase.
• KA origin videos massively outperform MG — "Video _ XPL04 KA #1" hits 48.53x ROAS at €7.98 CPP, the best unit economics in the account, while MG #1 barely breaks even.
❌ What's Not Working
• MG origin content gets clicks but not sales — "Video _ XPL04 MG #1" has 112.60% CTR but only 1.19x ROAS at €51.03 CPP. High engagement, zero purchase intent. The story or offer isn't landing.
• Origin storytelling in static format is flopping — "Static _ Origin #1" costs €47.26 per purchase, 3-4x worse than top performers. The USP isn't translating in this format.
• Generic messaging is dead on arrival — "Static _ General #1" spent €9 with zero purchases and "Static _ Barista #1" spent €6 with nothing. Vague doesn't convert specialty coffee buyers.
⬆ Double Down On
• Build more catalog carousel variants — espresso collection works, now launch single-origin collections, subscription starter packs, and seasonal curations in the same format.
• Expand the "Hold" urgency/scarcity messaging into new formats — this angle clearly resonates; create video versions, carousel adaptations, and new copy variants.
• Go deep on KA origin content — KA #1 is the best ROAS in the account at 48.53x. Create a full KA content series: static, longer video, UGC-style, carousel featuring KA beans specifically.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Pause "Video _ XPL04 MG #1" immediately — 1.19x ROAS is losing money after COGS. €51 CPP is unacceptable.
• Kill "Static _ General #1" — zero purchases, generic messaging doesn't work for a specialty brand. Stop running vague creative.
• Stop scaling "Static _ Origin #1" until the format is reworked — €47.26 CPP means the origin story isn't compelling enough in static. The story needs video or carousel to breathe.

• Lean into myth-busting and educational angles for Belgian market — EV charging misconceptions (cost, installation complexity, permits) are high-intent hooks that already show engagement.

Belgium

✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Investeren _ 2" is the undeniable workhorse — €14.41/lead for real estate is excellent, eating 99% of budget and converting consistently.
• Investment (investeren) angle clearly resonates with the Belgian target; the financial proposition of Waterzande is landing.
• Static format is proving sufficient for lead gen — no need for complex production to drive results at this CPR.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Static _ Investeren _ 3", "Static _ Investeren", and "Static _ Investeren _ 4" are completely starved — Meta's algorithm buried them instantly, meaning their hooks or visuals lost the first-impression battle against variant _2.
• Zero creative diversity: all four ads run the same "Investeren" angle. You're fishing in one pond with one bait — no lifestyle, no second-home, no kijkwoning, no emotional pull.
• No video or carousel formats tested at all — you're leaving the highest-engagement placements (Reels, Stories) underserved.
⬆ Double Down On
• Investment-led static creatives: iterate on _2's winning formula with fresh visuals (aerial Westerschelde shots, interior renders, rental yield callouts) to prevent fatigue.
• Introduce a lifestyle/emotional angle: waterfront rust, panoramic sunsets, "your weekends at the Westerschelde" — tap the second-home dreamers, not just spreadsheet investors.
• Launch kijkwoning-visit-specific ads with urgency and exclusivity hooks — these drive the highest-intent leads and the sales team can close them on-site.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the three zombie ads (_3, original, _4) in their current form — they'll never exit Meta's learning penalty with €2-3 spend and zero results.
• Stop running only one creative angle. A single "Investeren" theme across all ads is a concentration risk — one audience fatigue wave kills your entire pipeline.
• Stop ignoring video entirely — Belgian real estate competitors are flooding Reels and Stories with drone footage, and you're invisible there.

12 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

12 ads · €1726 spend · 274 results
✅ What's Working
• Naoshima #2 is the clear winner: 83 results at €5.40 CPR on highest spend—Meta's algorithm loves it and keeps feeding it impressions.
• The Sommerfeld series is quietly the most consistent: #3 (€5.78 CPR, 64 results) and #2 (€5.75 CPR, 14 results) both deliver sub-€6 leads without a single dud at scale.
• Bauhaus #1 posts the best CPR in the entire account at €5.17 but has only received €67—proof the algorithm found signal early, yet budget never followed.
❌ What's Not Working
• Bauhaus #5 absorbs the second-highest spend (€394) but delivers the worst CPR among scaled ads at €8.95—66% more expensive per lead than Naoshima #2. It's eating budget that should go to cheaper winners.
• Bauhaus #4 is a clear failure: €18.98 per single result after €19 spend. No creative signal, no reason to continue.
• Six creatives (Naoshima #1, #3, Sommerfeld #1, Bauhaus #3, #4) received under €20 combined—the algorithm never had a chance to optimise. These are data-starved, not data-informed decisions.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Naoshima- and Sommerfeld-style visuals—whatever tonal/compositional approach those series use is outperforming Bauhaus on efficiency by 20-40%. Create 2-3 net-new variants in each style.
• Introduce video and carousel formats immediately. The entire account is 100% static—there is zero format diversity. A single strong video walkthrough of a coastal penthouse could dramatically lower CPR and unlock new audience segments Meta can't reach with statics alone.
• Lean into the coastal-lifestyle + modernist-architecture intersection. The Belgian west coast is the emotional hook; pair it with golden-hour exteriors, aerial shots, and design-detail close-ups to differentiate from generic luxury real estate ads.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Pause Bauhaus #4 today. One lead at €18.98 with no creative signal—dead weight.
• Stop over-investing in Bauhaus #5 at €8.95 CPR. Redirect at least half its budget to Bauhaus #1 (€5.17 CPR) and Sommerfeld #2 (€5.75 CPR) which are starved of spend.
• Stop launching creatives and leaving them at €2-5 spend. Either commit €50+ to test a variant properly or don't launch it—micro-spend tests produce noise, not signal.

• Practical menu-integration angles consistently convert: "Menukaart #1" (€21.26), "Upgrade Brunch" (€21.98), and "Snel #1" (€24.76) all prove that showing B2B buyers exactly how açai fits their operation drives action.
❌ What's Not Working
• Consumer-facing creatives are total dead weight: "Static _ Bowl #1" burned €136 with zero results despite 281% CTR — massive curiosity clicks but a completely broken conversion path.
• Location-specific ads are DOA: "Watersportbaan #1" and "Deinze #1" have sub-3% CTR and zero results — hyper-local targeting generates neither engagement nor conversions.
• "Açai Koffiebar" is an expensive budget hog: it consumes the most spend (€466) but converts at €33.26 CPR — nearly double the cost of your top performer, silently draining the account.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more use-case/daypart B2B creatives modeled after "4 Momenten" — franchise the framework across breakfast, lunch, snack, and dessert occasions with fresh visuals.
• Scale the "Geen excuus" objection-busting angle with new variants — the €16 CPR proves the no-excuse psychology works on café and restaurant owners, it just needs real budget and creative iteration.
• Introduce video for B2B: every single ad is static — short-form prep demos and partner testimonials are completely untapped and will diversify creative fatigue risk.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all location-specific consumer ads immediately — "Watersportbaan #1" and "Deinze #1" are burning cash with sub-3% CTR and zero signal of life.
• Pause all consumer Bowl and Nutri creatives — they attract curiosity clicks but zero conversions, revealing a fundamental targeting or funnel disconnect that static tweaks won't fix.
• Stop feeding "Açai Koffiebar" disproportionate budget at €33.26 CPR when "4 Momenten #1" delivers the same result type at nearly half the cost.

✅ What's Working
• "New deliveries! Bekijk ons gamma..." is the only ad that converted — 11.17x ROAS at €76 CPP. 'New arrivals' framing plus Dutch product language drives action.
• High-CTR ads (500%+) cluster around specific product news: "New!! Delivery winter 2026", "It's thé time of thé season!!", "shop online:" — specificity and newness hook engagement.
• The single purchase proves the audience is there; the creative and campaign setup are the bottleneck, not the market.
❌ What's Not Working
• Generic boosted posts with zero copy ("Instagram-bericht", "Bericht: ''") are burning €270+ with zero purchases — these are vanity engagement traps, not sales drivers.
• URL-as-headline ads like "www.clothingdemasure.be" and "Instagram Post" waste €134 with no hook, no product, no reason to click through to buy.
• Nearly every ad appears to be a boosted post, not a conversion-optimized campaign — inflated CTRs signal engagement farming, not purchase intent.
⬆ Double Down On
• Build dedicated conversion-objective ads around the "New deliveries" angle that already converted — product drops with clear CTAs and shop-now buttons.
• Create purpose-built product showcase creatives in Dutch with pricing, urgency, and a direct path to checkout — stop relying on boosted organic posts.
• Develop a retargeting funnel for the high-engagement audience — hundreds of percent CTR means eyeballs exist, but no bottom-funnel ads exist to close them.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting generic Instagram posts with no copy, no CTA, and no product focus — they generate likes, not revenue.
• Kill all engagement-objective campaigns immediately and redirect 100% of budget to conversion-optimized campaigns.
• Stop splitting spend across 19 ads at €3-€80 each — consolidate into 3-4 strong conversion ads so Meta's algorithm can actually optimize.

❌ What's Not Working
• Zero results on both ads despite €91 total spend — the funnel is completely broken. Either the pixel/CAPI is misconfigured, the landing page kills intent, or the conversion event is wrong. CTR above 100% is mathematically impossible for standard link clicks, confirming a tracking catastrophe.
• No ROAS data on either ad means there is zero visibility into what's working at the revenue level — you're flying blind.
• Both ads are burning budget with no feedback loop. Without valid conversion data, Meta's algorithm cannot optimize delivery, so every euro spent is wasted learning nothing.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix tracking FIRST — no creative strategy matters until pixel, CAPI, and conversion events are verified firing correctly. This is a Day-0 blocker.
• Once tracking works, lean into the high-engagement hook style that's clearly generating clicks — the creative concept is resonating, the back-end is failing.
• Develop a B2B-specific funnel: workwear buyers need quotes, catalogs, or sample requests — not e-commerce checkout flows. Build lead-gen forms or quote-request landing pages.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all spend immediately until tracking is audited and confirmed working end-to-end. Every euro spent right now is literally untrackable waste.
• Stop optimizing for a conversion event that clearly isn't firing — switch to a verified micro-conversion or lead form while debugging.

✅ What's Working
• Vottem project is the clear winner — Vottem_apt (€17.52/result), Vottem_video (€18.89), Vottem_animatie (€25.60) all crushing it across every format.
• Brugge_penthouse dominates volume with 26 results at €33.92 — best scale candidate in the account.
• Animation and video formats consistently outperform static and slideshow across all projects (Vottem_animatie, Vottem_video, west_video).
❌ What's Not Working
• Slideshows are dead weight — georges_slideshow (€233, 0 results), wildebeek_slideshow_realisatie_variaties (€278, 0 results), stokerie_int_v2 (€181, 0 results). Three ads, €692 burned, zero leads.
• Charleroi market is bleeding money — Charleroi_native at €242.60/result and Charleroi_te-huur at €120/result suggest wrong audience, wrong creative, or wrong offer.
• Wildebeek project can't convert regardless of format — wildebeek_reel at €206/result, slideshow at €0/result. The project or positioning isn't resonating.
⬆ Double Down On
• Replicate the Vottem creative formula (video, animation, apartment-focused) across other projects — especially Blom and Brugge which show promise.
• Lean into video and animation as primary formats. Every project where video exists outperforms its static counterparts.
• Test the 'geen-registratie' (no-registration) low-friction approach from Awans (€52.52/result, 12 results) on other high-cost projects like Charleroi and Stokerie.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all slideshow formats immediately — €692 total spend, 0 total results. The format is broken for this audience.
• Kill Charleroi_native — €485 for 2 results is unacceptable. Rethink the entire Charleroi creative strategy before spending another euro.
• Kill georges_image_cta_v1_rem — the remarketing variant at €176/result with 1 result proves the pool is too small or the creative is fatigued.

• 11 of 20 ads produced exactly zero results. The account is bleeding budget on untested creative that should have been killed sooner.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Doorstromer-angle variations: this audience converts at 4-8x better CPR than anything else — iterate on copy, visuals, and formats aggressively.
• Clone the 'Copy' variant approach: both '-Copy' ads are the top two most efficient — reverse-engineer what changed (likely copy tweaks or hook) and apply to other audiences.
• Double the Alleenstaand #2 creative direction with fresh iterations: it's the only non-Doorstromer angle with proven volume at acceptable CPR.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill every V2 variant immediately — they consistently perform worse than originals across every audience segment, burning €1,100+ with terrible CPR.
• Kill all Jong Koppel ads — zero traction across 4 creatives and two naming conventions. This audience or angle is a dead end.
• Stop launching static-only creative — the entire account is static images with no format diversity, leaving massive optimization potential untapped.

3 ads · €239 spend · 4 results
✅ What's Working
• "PVC. VER.- PUB CONVERTION - 2026" delivers the lowest cost/result at €30.11 with the highest CTR (201.18%) — product-specific naming and the 2026 planning hook clearly resonate.
• The "2026" future-planning angle appears in both result-generating ads, suggesting urgency/forward-thinking framing drives action.
• Sky-high CTRs across all three ads (131–201%) indicate strong creative stopping power — the audience is engaging.
❌ What's Not Working
• "VERANDAS - PUB CONVERTIONS" burned €9 with zero results — generic product framing without a year hook or specificity fails to convert.
• "PERGOLAS - PUB CONVERTIONS - 2026" eats 83% of total budget but delivers a €66.65 cost/result — over 2x the PVC ad's efficiency, meaning pergola creative is leaking spend.
• Zero ROAS tracking across the entire account means you're optimizing blind — no idea if any of these leads are actually closing.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product-specific creative (PVC verandas, pergolas, conservatories each as standalone ads) — the PVC-specific ad proves niche beats generic.
• The "2026 planning" urgency frame — replicate this across every product line and test seasonal variants ("Book your spring 2026 install now").
• Lead-quality mechanisms: add qualifying questions to forms, test instant forms vs. landing pages, and implement offline conversion tracking to finally get ROAS data.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running generic "VERANDAS" ads without a specific hook or year anchor — they attract clicks but convert nobody.
• Stop scaling "PERGOLAS" at current creative — €66.65/lead is unsustainable without proof of downstream conversion.
• Stop flying without ROAS tracking — every euro spent without revenue attribution is a guess.

4 ads · €96 spend · 10 results
✅ What's Working
• CARPORTS is the clear winner: 8 results at €7.68 each on modest spend — proves carport demand is real and the creative converts.
• Conversion-optimized campaign structure (PUB CONVERTION naming) is the right call for this lead-gen vertical; PERGOLAS pulled 2 results even at higher CPR.
• Extremely high CTRs across all ads suggest strong thumb-stopping creative and solid audience-product fit in the Colmar/Liège market.
❌ What's Not Working
• PERGOLAS cost/result (€15.92) is 2x CARPORTS — the creative or offer isn't compelling enough to convert at the same efficiency.
• PVC- PER and VERANDAS PUB CONVERTION - Copie were starved of budget (€2 and €1) — impossible to learn anything; Meta's algorithm never exited learning phase.
• No ROAS tracking on any campaign is a massive blind spot — you're optimizing on leads with zero visibility into revenue, risking scale on unprofitable traffic.
⬆ Double Down On
• Carport-specific creatives: the product clearly resonates — produce 3-4 new angles (before/after installs, pricing anchors, seasonal urgency) and scale spend to €30+/day.
• Give verandas and PVC real budgets (€15-20/day minimum) — the high CTR hints at interest but zero results at €1-2 spend is meaningless data.
• Install offline conversion tracking or CRM-linked ROAS measurement immediately — without it you're flying blind on which leads actually close.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop launching campaigns at €1-2/day — it wastes money and teaches nothing. Minimum €10/day or don't bother.
• Kill the habit of duplicating campaigns without differentiation ("Copie" suffix on VERANDAS) — test distinct creative angles, not carbon copies.

• "Static _ Veranda _ Lifestyle #1 - Copy" (€67 variant) is the only ad producing results — 3 at €22.45 CPA, proving lifestyle framing resonates for veranda leads.
• High reported CTRs across all ads (56–118%) suggest the creative hooks grab attention; the veranda visual style is at least stopping thumbs.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Static _ Veranda _ Quality #1 - Copy" spent €38 with zero results — the 'quality' angle is too abstract and fails to convert curiosity into action.
• The second "Static _ Veranda _ Lifestyle #1 - Copy" (€66 variant) burned nearly identical budget to its twin but produced zero results — duplicate naming makes optimization impossible and signals sloppy account hygiene.
• Total 30-day spend of €171 across only 3 near-identical statics is dangerously under-diversified. This account is flying blind with no ROAS tracking, no creative variety, and no learning volume.
⬆ Double Down On
• Lifestyle-first veranda creative: show people actually living in the space — dining, reading, hosting. The only results came from this angle.
• Lead-gen-specific formats: carousel walkthroughs, before/after transformations, and short video tours that pre-qualify intent before the click.
• Urgency and social proof hooks: testimonials from French homeowners, local project showcases, seasonal pricing angles (spring/summer installation windows).
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the 'Quality' messaging angle as a primary hook — it's generic and produced nothing. Quality belongs in body copy, not headlines.
• Kill the practice of duplicating ads with identical names. It wrecks reporting and splits learning. Rename and restructure immediately.
• Kill running this account without verified ROAS or CPA goals. Flag to stakeholders: 'MULTI COMPTE' may be a shared holding account — confirm ownership, pixel setup, and conversion tracking before spending another euro.

• Every "PUB" prefix ad underperforms or flatlines: PUB VERANDAS 2 has TWO variants with ZERO results (€122 wasted), PUB CARPORT 1 at €53/result, PUB PVC 3 at €46/result. "PUB" = lazy static creative that doesn't convert.
• RJF variants are disasters — PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_RJF7 burned €414 for 4 results (€103.56 CPR) and VERANDA_CARROUSEL_RJF8 spent €43 for zero results. Whatever "RJF" targeting or creative variant means, kill it.
• PVC category is bleeding: PVC VERANCOBEL (€47.44 CPR) and PUB PVC 3 (€46.48 CPR) suggest the PVC offer or creative doesn't resonate at all.
⬆ Double Down On
• Video-first creative across ALL product lines — video is 40-50% more efficient than static/carousel on CPR. Produce video for carports, pergolas, and PVC immediately.
• Carousel format for pergolas specifically — PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_MUTLI4 proves carousel + pergola = volume. Test new carousel angles (lifestyle, before/after, seasonal).
• Verancobel brand-led creative — both Verancobel-named ads (video veranda + PVC) have the highest CTRs (271% and 248%), suggesting brand recognition lifts engagement. Lean into branded creative.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All "PUB" prefix ads — they are consistently the worst performers across every product category. Zero creative differentiation, zero results.
• RJF variants immediately — PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_RJF7 and VERANDA_CARROUSEL_RJF8 are burning budget with abysmal or zero conversions.
• Duplicate underperforming CARPORTS variant at €37.91 CPR — consolidate budget into the €19.48 CPR winner instead of spreading across three carport ads.

❌ What's Not Working

⬆ Double Down On

• Conversion-optimized campaign structure: stop boosting posts. Build dedicated purchase-objective campaigns with proper pixel events and product pages.
• Lokeren store buzz is real — leverage that local energy with geo-targeted offers that drive both foot traffic AND online conversions with trackable codes.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting organic 'Bericht' posts as ads. They have no CTA, no landing page, no conversion intent. This is lighting money on fire.
• Kill weekly schedule posts ('Deze week kan je hier terecht!') as paid ads immediately — this is Google Maps content, not advertising.
• Stop running Event ads without a conversion mechanism — 'Feestelijke opening' and 'XXL STOCK SALE' need trackable offers or they're vanity spend.
